text.p: Accor SA chairman Jean-Marc Espalioux forecast in an interview to appear on Saturday the hotel group's 1997 profits would show good progress.
"I maintain net profit will show good progress," he told the Journal des Finances.
He said he could make no precise forecast until he saw the results of a review of the group's hotel assets being conducted in the second half.
For 1996, Accor reported net attributable profit rose 14.6 percent to 1.06 billion francs, helped by gains from the sale and leaseback of hotels.

Espalioux said 1997 net profit would reflect three main elements -- a 20 percent rise in pre-tax, pre-exceptional profit, a one billion franc capital gain from sale of its Compass shares and the accounting results of the review of its hotel assets.
He said he expected the group to top 10 percent in return on capital employed (ROCE) in the coming months, thanks to the recovery of hotels at the high end of the range.

"For the future, the projects (in hotels, casinos, new areas) we have been examining since the start of the year have for the most part provisional ROCE equal to 15 percent, sometimes much higher," he said
He said with Accor's majority holding in SPIC (Societe de Participations et d'Investissements de Casinos), the group was now a "major player" in the casino field.
In the United States, he did not rule out an alliance with a hotel group for its Motel 6 chain but the group expected to develop its franchise operations above all.
"We will have 40 franchised motels at the end of 1997 and we expect to reach 50 a year from 1998," he said.
